history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its efforts to increase gender and geographical representation on the three rosters.
history.administration_response: The electoral roster is open for applications from all eligible and interested candidates and several efforts have been made in recent years to diversify the roster in terms of gender, language balance and geographic representation. Every few years, roster campaigns are organized with the aim of adding new areas of expertise to the existing pool of experts and increasing the gender and language balance and geographic representation. While no new roster campaigns have been conducted since the recommendation was put in place (given that, as indicated, such campaigns take place every few years), the Electoral Assistance Division in the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs will ensure that this recommendation serves as key guidance in conducting the next campaign and will proactively engage in measures to increase geographical representation and gender balance on the roster, as far as possible. With respect to the roster for the Security Council subsidiary organs, the Security Council Subsidiary Organs Branch of the Security Council Affairs Division remains committed to increasing the number of women serving on panels of experts to at least 50 per cent (in support of the Secretary-General’s goal of achieving system-wide gender parity by 2028, as well as the Department’s women and peace and security policy). The Department will also work on improving the number of women from all regional groups on the rosters and the overall geographical representation on the rosters. In this context, the Branch has collaborated closely with the Office of Human Resources in the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance to conduct strategic outreach (including through United Nations social media) to attract candidates for expert positions. In the future, the Branch will enhance its strategic outreach, including through its gender focal point, to Member States and other relevant stakeholders so as to attract suitable and diverse candidates. In addition, as set out in the audit responses of the Policy and Mediation Division, following the successful completion of the annual rigorous, in-depth assessment process concluded by the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) in late 2021, two new individuals were added to the Mediation Support Unit roster of the approved Standby Team of Senior Mediation Advisers. As at 7 March 2022, the Unit’s updated roster of approved Standby Team Advisers, including a gender and geographical breakdown of its members, was provided in the Division’s audit responses. As part of this 2021 assessment process, carried out by UNOPS, the Unit encouraged roster candidacies from underrepresented countries by sending a note verbale from the Division inviting all permanent missions in New York to consider encouraging their nationals to apply.
history.board_assessment: Given that efforts are still needed to improve gender balance and geographical representation on the three rosters, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

All current members of the pool of experts are active, can modify their profiles online and can apply for vacancies on the platform. Going forward, at the end of each calendar year, the Security Council Affairs Division will invite all members of the pool of experts to update their profiles, as appropriate.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify its efforts to increase gender and geographical representation on the three rosters.
history.administration_response: We request the closure of this recommendation since it has been overtaken by new events related to the Secretary-General’s new policy on global roster building which addresses the issue of gender and geographical representation in the rosters through a United Nations system-wide approach. This new comprehensive approach will also include the electoral roster, as well as other such rosters. In the meantime, the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs has continued its efforts to improve the number of women from all regional groups in the sanctions roster, as well as the overall geographical representation. In June 2023, the Department, through the Security Council Affairs Division, participated in a virtual career fair for nationals from the Middle East and North Africa regions and, in October 2023, at a virtual career fair for women in senior positions. The Security Council Affairs Division also briefed representatives of the African Group on the recruitment process for members of sanctions expert groups on 6 July 2023. To further strengthen gender and geographical representation with respect to mediation, the Department conducted its annual review of the roster of approved standby team advisers in December 2023. The Department reiterates that the majority of mediation support assignments are conducted by the full-time standby team, drawn each year from the roster with a focus on achieving gender parity and geographical balance. Since 2020, the standby team has had full gender parity each year. In addition, from 2023-2024, experts serving on the Team have had the following nationalities: Colombia (1), Ghana (1), Ireland (1), Kenya (1), Lebanon (1), South Africa (2), Spain (1), Türkiye (1), Uganda (1), United States (2). In 2023, 81 per cent of all assignments have been conducted by the full-time team.
history.board_assessment: Given the development of a new Secretary-General policy on Global Roster Building, which aims to address rostering issues including gender and geographical balance within the UN system- wide, and considering the management’s ongoing efforts to enhance representation of women from all regional groups as well as overall geographical diversity in the sanctions roster, Single Electoral roster, and Standby Team Advisers roster, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
